Exhaustion, guilt and no life of their own
(23 of 55 threads)

It happens (from the quotes):
“Right now I’m resentful and really don’t understand why I can’t get over it and just be there for her the way a daughter should be.” (agi-499699)
“But the idea of leaving my mom somewhere and her begging me to not leave her, I get sick whenever I think about it.” (alz-77432)
ASSUMPTION: We want the caregiver to have breaks and support so caring does not cost them their health, job or relationships.

ASSUMPTION:
• The caregiver can step away for a few hours and knows the person is looked after
• The caregiver can find support at times that fit a working life
• The caregiver is not the only one carrying the load

Dementia behavior and hard conversations
(14 of 55 threads)

It happens (from the quotes):
“We have tried many times to take her to lunch, shopping etc. but it always ends with her request to be taken "home" to see her dogs.” (alz-77399)
“At first we were telling her that he died but that would cause a meltdown every time and it was heartbreaking.” (alz-77460)
ASSUMPTION: We want caregivers to know what to say and do when the person is anxious, angry or confused, so visits and calls do not end in distress.

ASSUMPTION:
• A caregiver gets through a hard call or visit without a meltdown
• A caregiver knows when a behavior is the illness and when it needs a doctor
• Repeated calls do not take over the caregiver's workday

Money, legal papers and facility bills
(11 of 55 threads)

It happens (from the quotes):
“the house needs several repairs before we can put it on the market, including interior painting, ceiling and window frame repairs from previous water leaks, and basement mold remediation.” (alz-77396)
“the financial dept where she is a resident had me signing documents to apply for medicaid right now, this minute because the house hasn't sold as quick as I thought it would” (agi-499298)
ASSUMPTION: We want families to understand and control money, legal papers and facility bills, so nothing is signed under pressure or paid wrongly.

ASSUMPTION:
• A caregiver knows what a facility charges and why
• A caregiver can apply for benefits without being rushed
• The person with legal authority and the relatives who help can see the same account information

Relatives do not help, or block each other
(10 of 55 threads)

It happens (from the quotes):
“When I broke down and begged them to help me, younger sister told me, "We all make our choices."” (agi-499771)
“struggle with sisters who live near us but don’t help even after I have asked.” (alz-77423)
ASSUMPTION: We want relatives to share the load and the information, without conflict or going through lawyers.

ASSUMPTION:
• A sibling who lives far away knows what is needed and does their part
• A relative with legal authority cannot keep others from the person without a reason they can see
• Decisions about the parent are made together

Medicines, eating and personal care
(8 of 55 threads)

It happens (from the quotes):
“It was a lot of work every morning of cleaning him up, and doing all the laundry.” (agi-499448)
“Dad will definitely take them once he remembers to pick up the pillbox.” (alz-77417)
ASSUMPTION: We want the person to take their medicines, eat and stay clean without a daily fight and without the caregiver doing it all alone.

ASSUMPTION:
• The caregiver knows whether a dose was taken or missed
• Morning and night personal care does not exhaust the caregiver
• The person eats enough

Choosing and arranging a place for them
(6 of 55 threads)

It happens (from the quotes):
“My Mom had agreed to move into AL and then turned around yesterday (about a week before it was time to move) and says 100% no way.” (alz-77401)
“So far I haven't even found a nursing home with physical therapy options that will accept her having medicare, all are refusing her.” (agi-499762)
ASSUMPTION: We want families to arrange a move to assisted living or a nursing home with confidence, without the person being forced or tricked.

ASSUMPTION:
• A family can compare places and costs before a crisis
• The person has a say in the move
• A move is planned for a time when it can go well

Staying safe at home
(6 of 55 threads)

It happens (from the quotes):
“She has walked, "jogged", alone, up and down the street we live on every day and only recently, and on only one occasion (that we know of) gotten disoriented and lost.” (alz-77129)
“My mom wandered from her usual walking route and was brought home by police after a neighbor recognized a disoriented senior on a bench in our neighborhood.” (alz-77393)
ASSUMPTION: We want the person to stay safe at home without constant watching.

ASSUMPTION:
• The caregiver knows if the person left home or fell
• Hazards such as the stove do not cause harm
• A person who wanders is found quickly

Getting answers from doctors and hospitals
(4 of 55 threads)

It happens (from the quotes):
“His diagnosis was missed by several doctors and with HIPPA, if it was caught, no one knew so we could start getting help sooner.” (alz-77385)
“I'm starting to realize what a disadvantage we've been at, having had so little information.” (alz-77005)
ASSUMPTION: We want families to get clear information and quick callbacks from doctors, hospitals and programs.

ASSUMPTION:
• A caregiver gets a diagnosis sooner
• A caregiver gets a callback within days, not weeks
• Privacy rules do not leave the caregiver without answers

Being far away and not knowing what is happening
(2 of 55 threads)

It happens (from the quotes):
“I’m POA to my elderly mother who lives out of state and I have been dealing with missing information from people close to her who live in her town which is causing me a great deal of stress” (agi-499712)
“I feel like I can’t even call her (I don’t live nearby) because I will just be a reminder of my dad.” (alz-77460)
ASSUMPTION: We want relatives who live far away to stay informed and able to help.

ASSUMPTION:
• A caregiver far away has the information the people near the parent have
• Calls and visits from far away still help the parent
spouse:
Exhaustion, loneliness and own health
(22 of 54 threads)

It happens (from the quotes):
“I am tired of doing it all - cooking, cleaning, daily laundry, paying bills, grocery shoping, doctors appointments, I’m even tired of crying everyday” (alz-77470)
“Now, when my help is here and I run an errand I dread going back.” (alz-77364)
ASSUMPTION: We want the spouse caregiver to keep their own health and have someone to lean on.

ASSUMPTION:
• The caregiver gets regular breaks
• The caregiver has someone to talk to
• The caregiver's own medical needs are not put off

Dementia behavior and hard conversations
(18 of 54 threads)

It happens (from the quotes):
“She is determined to stay independent and takes offense to any questions or reminders about medications and other normal daily questions or reminders.” (alz-77457)
“As my husband's mixed dementia got worse and his behavior became more aggressive I consented when his doctor suggested more drugs.” (alz-77414)
ASSUMPTION: We want caregivers to handle agitation, repeated questions and refusal without anger or exhaustion.

ASSUMPTION:
• The caregiver finds something that calms the person when the usual tactics stop working
• Evening restlessness does not end the day in conflict
• The caregiver knows when to ask a doctor about behavior or medicine

Personal care and medicines
(12 of 54 threads)

It happens (from the quotes):
“She also forgets when she has a glass of wine if we go out to dinner and comes home and pours another.” (alz-77112)
“DH is up and down from about 3.30pm every night, a few overshoots in the bathroom” (alz-77454)
ASSUMPTION: We want bathing, toileting, medicines and eating to be manageable at home.

ASSUMPTION:
• Night-time incontinence does not wreck the caregiver's sleep
• The person takes medicine without a fight
• Doctors can see the readings or notes the caregiver keeps

Safety when they are alone or out
(9 of 54 threads)

It happens (from the quotes):
“when there’s no family restroom and my DH has to go into the men’s room by himself and there’s no other men going on or coming out” (alz-77263)
“I'm still worried about her safety when I'm away as well as her frantic phone calls minutes after I leave” (alz-77407)
ASSUMPTION: We want the person to be safe when the caregiver is not with them and when they go out.

ASSUMPTION:
• The caregiver can leave the house briefly knowing the person is safe
• Public places work for a couple, for example restrooms
• A conversation about driving can happen in time

Aides, hospice and trusting others
(8 of 54 threads)

It happens (from the quotes):
“when I was gone for a few hours at a time, she had nothing to hold her accountable, she didn't do anything at all.” (agi-499829)
“The very first day, a lady showed up at 8:00am thinking she was going to give me, rather than my wife a shower.” (alz-77347)
ASSUMPTION: We want caregivers to trust paid help and know what happened while they were away.

ASSUMPTION:
• The caregiver knows how an aide's visit went
• A hospice or aide visit happens as promised
• The caregiver can leave the person with others for a few hours

Placing them and care costs
(7 of 54 threads)

It happens (from the quotes):
“It is a huge decision for us, as what will I have after he’s gone? And living on my income if/when he is in MC will be tight!” (alz-77354)
“When they started leaving her in her room all day in the same dirty clothes, I found another place as quickly as I could.” (alz-77364)
ASSUMPTION: We want families to place a spouse in memory care at the right time, in a good place, and to be able to afford it.

ASSUMPTION:
• The caregiver can judge when home care is no longer enough
• The caregiver can find a good place and pay for it
• Care in the new place meets the spouse's needs

Money, scams and bills
(6 of 54 threads)

It happens (from the quotes):
“I am so overwhelmed with his bills- left so unintended- and the lack of addressing so many things when he walked out of his job” (alz-77428)
“We are now living the results of DW in early stages getting scammed multiple times, turning our finances upside down.” (alz-77411)
ASSUMPTION: We want the spouse's money, bills and exposure to scams under control.

ASSUMPTION:
• The caregiver can take over bills that were left behind
• The person cannot be scammed or overspend
• Care costs can be planned

Diagnosis and doctor delays
(4 of 54 threads)

It happens (from the quotes):
“DW finally getting actual sustained treatment after nine months of insurance changes, delays, one rogue neuro PA, etc.” (alz-77371)
“There’s something off with some of his cognitive abilities but we do not have a why or what it is.” (alz-77409)
ASSUMPTION: We want a diagnosis and treatment without long waits.

ASSUMPTION:
• A person with new symptoms sees a specialist within weeks
• The family understands what is wrong

Relatives and others not helping or criticizing
(3 of 54 threads)

It happens (from the quotes):
“the bigger problem for me is his daughter and exwife that have given me more grief than anyone else. They aren't supportive, they degrade me” (alz-77427)
“those I held near and dear are “ too busy” to lend a hand, give me a call, or ask how I’m doing.” (alz-77470)
ASSUMPTION: We want family and friends to support the caregiver, not criticize.

ASSUMPTION:
• The caregiver has family who step in
• Criticism from relatives does not add to the stress
